0.long_answer: The condition is known as premature ovarian insufficiency, which is also referred to as premature ovarian failure. It is characterized by the partial or complete loss of normal ovarian function before the age of 40. This results in reduced estrogen production and elevated gonadotropin levels, and can lead to secondary amenorrhea—a condition where menstruation ceases after it has previously occurred. Premature ovarian insufficiency affects about 1% of women and can be caused by various factors including genetic abnormalities (such as Turner syndrome), autoimmune disorders, and certain medical treatments like chemotherapy, among others.
